paragraphs.text: A [red tea](red:definition) made in 2023 on [Taiwan](taiwan:on-a-label). Red tea is the fully oxidised tea that English calls black. The record names only the island, not a mountain or township, so where on it the garden lies is not known. The island is known above all for [oolong](taiwan:known-for), and it [turned to black tea](taiwan:history) under Japanese rule, when red tea was first made at [Yuchi](red:history) near Sun Moon Lake.

Red tea has no tradition of [ageing](red:ageing). Sealed, it keeps its quality for about a year and a half to three years. At three years this tea sits at the far end of that span, so it is one to drink now rather than to keep.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
